newsitem.title: UK: AMP preparing bid for Scottish Amicable - paper.
newsitem.headline: AMP preparing bid for Scottish Amicable - paper.

text.p: Australian Mutual Provident (AMP) is expected to sign a confidentiality agreement allowing it to check Scottish Amicable's books in preparation for a bid on the life insurance company, according to The Scotsman newspaper.

AMP, which recently announced its own plans to de-mutualise, already owns UK life insurer Pearl Assurance, and has stated a wish too spend between one billion stg and 2.5 billion stg to grow its presence in the UK or the US.
The newspaper quoted AMP chief executive George Trumbull as reiterating this objective on Australian television on Sunday.
"I'd like to believe we'd make an acquisition, the prices a pretty steep right now, particularly in the U.S." Trumbull said according to The Scotsman.
"We're of a mind that overpaying doesn't make much sense so I think it depends on the market and the opportunities," he said.
Speculation began at the end of January when Abbey National made 1.4 million bid for Scottish amicable which was turned down.
